Alex — following up with technical clarifications and requested evidence pointers. I'm Marcus (Head of Security Ops). Below are the inline answers to the most technical items in your SSQ (pulled from the PDF for convenience).

1) Key custody & KMS
- Hosted: Redwood-managed AWS KMS (multi-tenant keyring). Keys are HSM-backed; Redwood holds key material and enforces strict access via IAM, KMS grant policies, and least-privilege service principals. We rotate CMKs on a 12-month schedule and maintain rotation artifact logs.
- Dedicated/Private: BYOK supported. Customers request key import via our control plane; we support AWS KMS imported keys and external HSMs for on-prem Private deployments. BYOK onboarding is gated by an HSM review and key escrow policy.
- Evidence: SOC 2 control mapping and a KMS attestation deck (link provided in our response PDF).

2) Subprocessors & access to raw inputs
- Subprocessors with potential access to unredacted inputs are marked in the attached CSV. Generally, only the inference runtime (Redwood runtime) and short-lived GPU workers see plaintext inputs during inference. Persistent stores (analytics, logging) receive either metadata or hashed/sampled payloads unless customer chooses to persist full transcripts.
- We use a mix of cloud providers for hosting (AWS, GCP) and partner-managed logging/observability (Datadog for metrics, S3/BigQuery for long-term telemetry depending on deployment). The CSV includes whether each vendor may access unredacted inputs.

3) Cross-border transfers
- For EU-related accounts we provide SCCs; customers can also request data localization options (pin to region) on Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request contractual export controls during onboarding.

4) Telemetry & PII handling
- Default telemetry (metrics, traces) excludes full prompts. Customers may enable detailed logging; if enabled, there are config flags to redact or hash prompt text before persistence. Retention settings are configurable per account.

5) Evidence & audit artifacts
- SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we provide redacted network diagrams and an operations playbook on request. The SSQ PDF we returned includes links to a shared Drive for secure evidence delivery.

Next steps: if OmniMed needs a formal KMS attestation letter (BYOK flow or Redwood-managed separation of duties), we can schedule a short call and produce a signed attestation within 3 business days.

Alex — quick answers below, and happy to set up a 30m call if you prefer to walk through these live.

- Telemetry: by default, our analytics pipeline stores observability metadata (timings, error traces, token counts). Full prompt/response text is not included in standard telemetry. If a customer opts into detailed logging, we provide ingestion-time redaction hooks: (1) prefix hashing (irreversible HMAC of the first N tokens), (2) token-level scrub rules (PII pattern removal), or (3) no-collection mode which bypasses ingestion entirely for sensitive routes. We can enable 2) or 3) for OmniMed account-level policy prior to production.

- Subprocessors marked as "may access unredacted inputs": the logging partner (internal name LogFlux) only sees unredacted inputs in Dedicated environments where customers have explicitly enabled full-session logging. For Hosted customers, we never send raw prompts to external logging partners without an explicit customer setting. The QA vendor (PromptLab Services) receives sampled transcripts for model evaluation in a controlled staging environment and only under a narrow NDA and data minimization controls. We can hand you the vendor-specific confidentiality addendum and add them to the DPA exhibit as a conditional subprocessor — or we can add an extra contractual clause requiring pseudo-anonymization prior to sharing.

Proposed action:
- We will mark the OmniMed account with "no-collection" for telemetry by default and document the setting in the DPA exhibit.
- We'll attach the vendor confidentiality addenda and add a clause for pseudo-anonymization for any QA sampling.
